tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Inverse Function Theorem for Manifolds]

↗ lem:local-diffeomorphism-from-invertible-differential

1. chA:A.14

Suppose $M$ and $N$ are smooth manifolds and $F: M o N$ is a smooth map. If the linear map $dF_p$ is invertible at some point $p \in M$, then there exist connected neighborhoods $U_0$ of $p$ and $V_0$ of $F(p)$ such that $F|_{U_0}: U_0 o V_0$ is a diffeomorphism.

Proof

↗ lem:local-diffeomorphism-from-invertible-differential By Lemma 5 there are open sets $U i p$ and $V i F(p)$ such that $F|_U : U o V$ is a diffeomorphism. Let $U_0$ be the connected component of $p$ in $U$. A smooth manifold is locally connected, being locally homeomorphic to a normed space, in which the balls are convex and hence connected; therefore $U_0$ is open, and by construction it is connected and contains $p$. Put $V_0 = F(U_0)$. Then $V_0$ is open, being the image of an open subset of $U$ under the diffeomorphism $F|_U$, it is connected as the continuous image of a connected set, and it contains $F(p)$. Finally $F|_{U_0} : U_0 o V_0$ is a diffeomorphism, being the restriction of the diffeomorphism $F|_U$ to an open subset of its domain and to the image of that subset.

□

The proof of the manifold statement rests on the corresponding statement for the coordinate representation, together with the fact that invertibility of a bounded operator is an open condition.
